```{r}
library(tidyverse) 
library(knitr)

candidate_paths <- c(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  "../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv"
)

data_path <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)][1]
if (is.na(data_path)) {
  stop("Could not find examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv")
}

nhanes <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Define Analysis Cohort
We decided to keep adults age 20-80 (inclusive) for the analysis. This allows us to summarize adult BMI summaries while avoiding children, adolescents, and extremely elderly records into our classroom table

```{r}
analysis_df <- nhanes |>
  filter(Age >= 20, Age <= 80)

cohort_counts <- tibble(
  step = c("Prepared CSV rows", "Rows after age 20-80 restriction"),
  n = c(nrow(nhanes), nrow(analysis_df))
)

kable(cohort_counts)
```

## Missingness Check
```{r}
key_vars <- c("BMI", "Age", "IncomeGroup", "Gender", "Race", "Cycle")

missingness <- tibble(variable = key_vars) |>
  mutate(
    missing_n = vapply(analysis_df[key_vars], function(x) sum(is.na(x)), numeric(1)),
    missing_percent = round(100 * missing_n / nrow(analysis_df), 1)
  )

kable(missingness) 
## Both BMI and IncomeGroup have missing values, so we
## will filter out those records for the Table 1 style 
## summary.
```

## Table 1 Style Description Summary
```{r}
mean_sd <- function(x) {
  sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))
}

table1 <- analysis_df |>
    filter(!is.na(BMI) & !is.na(IncomeGroup)) |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    `BMI, mean (SD)` = mean_sd(BMI),
    `Age, mean (SD)` = mean_sd(Age),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## Filter is seen above given the missingness table

kable(table1)
write_csv(table1, "table1.csv")


## AI use note: AI was used to help draft code to transfer
## the table1 created in the terminal to a CSV file. The 
## AI prompt was: Can you create a code that will create 
## a csv file called "table1.csv" derived from the table 
## 1 style description summary in the eda-note.qmd lines 
## 50-65. Verified: Checked the file table1.csv file and 
## confirmed that it has the same information as the 
## output of the Table 1 descripion summary.
```

## Methods note
We used the prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom CSV 
snapshot. The analysis cohort included records with age 
20-80. We summarized BMI and age by income group using 
unweighted descriptive statistics. Missing values were 
checked before summarizing. These summaries describe the 
prepared class dataset and should not be interpreted as 
causal effects or population estimates.
